newsitem.title: USA: Humana sees continued membership fall in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Humana sees continued membership fall in Q1.

text.p: Humana Inc said total commercial membership fell by 87,500 members in January, and it expects membership to decrease by another 115,000 during the remainder of the first quarter, primarily as a result of the sale of its Washington D.C. and Alabama operations.

Humana said commercial membership declined by 31,600 members during 1996's fourth quarter, due to its planned exit from unprofitable markets and pricing of commercial products at rates designed to improve profitability.
Earlier, it reported lower fourth quarter and full year operating and net income despite higher premium revenues.

It said commercial membership fell by 69,100 members in 1996. For both the fourth quarter and year, membership losses from the exit of unprofitable markets and the "proper pricing" of commercial products were partially offset by increases in the small group (former EMPHESYS) platform.
"Our plans to withdraw from certain markets and price business commensurate with the underlying risk are proceeding on schedule," said company president Gregory Wolf.

"Commercial membership will decrease an additional 115,000 members during the remainder of the first quarter, primarily as a result of the sale of our Washington D.C. and Alabama operations. After these two sales are completed, commercial membership should begin to grow modestly," Wolf said.

Humana said medical membership at December 31 totaled a record 4.9 million members, compared with 3.8 million members at December 31, 1995, primarily due to the addition of Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Uniformed Services (CHAMPUS) eligible members.
Medicare risk membership increased 17,100 members during the fourth quarter, and grew by 54,100 members or 17 percent in 1996.
